note: Authored. A project is a named design goal with its subsystems by scale, the models and media that exist for each, and the gaps. The Project record schema exists, and each project here has a validated draft file. This file is the site's own projection: a project is a stored Project only when its entry names a live_project_id, and none does yet. Until then each is an authored proposal.

projects.title: Flying fish
projects.goal: Engineer toward a vertebrate glider reachable from a beloniform ancestor, and make every missing bridge between scales visible.
projects.summary: Eleven scales from molecule to ecology. Recorded models exist at four of them, a bounded constraint solver and illustrative print forms at the organism and organ scales; most scales hold only a stated gap.

molecular.gap: No molecular model output exists. Daane 2021 shows a zebrafish interaction that phenocopies flying-fish fin proportion; transfer to a halfbeak is unestablished.

macromolecular.gap: No structure or affinity model is attached. The stopped KCNE1 protocol shows what an uncovered structure does to a test.

cellular.gap: The SBML replay is a two-cell abstraction; it says nothing about fin cells.

tissue.gap: Reaction-diffusion fields are generic pattern models, not a fin tissue model.

organ.gap: A scoped elastic surrogate; how real fin rays load and bend is not modelled.

neural.gap: Simulated control models only, with no neural recording and no Exocoetidae calibration. The escape-to-launch chain (M1) is driven by power-capped caudal thrust (M2, which extends behavior-cpg), and a glide pitch/roll stabiliser with sensing delays (M3) runs on the r3-daane geometry. What a nervous system would have to implement, and what these models do not establish: engineering/neuro/NEURAL_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

organism.gap: The glide model uses assumed coefficients; the corrected common-launch comparison found no robust winner across the tested scenarios.

developmental.gap: No developmental model links adult proportions to a programme.

ecological.gap: Reachability from a halfbeak ancestor is unestablished; no evolutionary model is attached.

projects.title: Contractile tissue microcarrier
projects.goal: Ask one question about a Xenopus-inspired contractile tissue construct: how does a chosen actuation pattern turn into deformation, and how much of that deformation becomes net motion?
projects.summary: A bounded proposal. A generic soft-body mechanics runner and existing cell-scale tools are named as instruments. No simulation of this construct exists in this node yet, and no frog or fish parameter is used.

context.base: The source context is cell constructs made from Xenopus laevis (frog) cells. This project takes the abstract question only: actuation pattern, deformation, motion. It takes no frog parameter.
not_this: A designed living organism or a release claim
A fish tissue, or part of the flying-fish design

scales.role: Where force comes from: contractile or ciliated cells (the sources report ciliary locomotion; contraction is this project's modelling choice)
A construct of many cells as a deformable body under an actuation pattern
Construct-level shape change and net displacement (an organ-scale body, not an organism)

tools.use: Cellular Potts engine already run here. It shows how a cell-level rule is exposed to a tissue-level readout.
tools.limit: A generic growth and cytokine example. It has no contraction and no elastic modulus.

tools.use: A cellular adhesion clutch render. Shows how cell-scale force is represented here.
tools.limit: A render of one simulation. No transfer to a construct is attempted.

tools.use: Bioelectric patch with gap-junction controls, as one possible upstream of contraction.
tools.limit: Not calibrated to any cell. The voltage-to-contraction link is not established.

virtual.name: Soft-voxel actuation comparison
virtual.status: proposed; no runner or result is in this node yet
virtual.plan: A finite set of actuation patterns over a small voxel body, with a passive arm, a mirrored arm and dt and mesh refinement. Generic mechanics only.

physical.name: Construct motion and strain tracking
physical.plan: Time-lapse tracking of centroid displacement and contraction strain, with an inhibited or passive control arm.
physical.needs: Stiffness measured on the same construct type (for example by micropipette aspiration or AFM) before any modulus is used.

sources.cite: Kriegman S, Blackiston D, Levin M, Bongard J (2020). A scalable pipeline for designing reconfigurable organisms. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 117(4):1853-1859.
sources.note: Abstract read from PubMed. Full text not read here.

sources.cite: Blackiston D, Lederer E, Kriegman S, Garnier S, Bongard J, Levin M (2021). A cellular platform for the development of synthetic living machines. Sci Robot 6(52):eabf1571.
sources.note: Abstract read from PubMed. Full text not read here.

claims.text: AI methods design candidate lifeforms in silico for a desired function, and designs judged transferable are then built with a cell-based construction toolkit.
claims.quote: transferable designs are then created using a cell-based construction toolkit

claims.text: Xenopus laevis cell constructs move by cilia on their surface and heal after damage. Their locomotion is ciliary, so a contraction-driven model is a different mechanism from the one this abstract reports.
claims.quote: coordinated locomotion via cilia present on their surface

missing_couplings: Cell actuation (contraction or cilia) to tissue stress: no sourced parameter and no model.
Tissue stress to construct deformation: needs an elastic modulus of the construct. None is measured here.
Deformation to net motion in a fluid or on a surface: not modelled.
Simulated design to built construct: the source reports a pipeline, not a transfer rule for any runner in this node.

endpoints.text: With actuation off, from zero initial velocity and a settled force-balanced shape, with no external flow or forcing, a defined reference frame and after a stated transient window, net displacement is zero to numerical tolerance.
endpoints.falsifier: A nonzero passive displacement under those stated conditions triggers diagnosis of the setup or the runner. If a condition was not met, the control is restated, not read as a defect. No other endpoint is read until it is resolved.

endpoints.text: Two predeclared patterns with equal total actuation give net displacements that differ by more than a dt or mesh refinement changes either one.
endpoints.falsifier: If the difference is smaller than the refinement change, no pattern-to-motion statement is made.

endpoints.text: A mirrored pattern on a symmetric body gives the mirrored displacement.
endpoints.falsifier: A failure marks an anisotropy artifact in the body or the solver.

open_questions: Which actuation to deformation relation, if any, is shared by a soft-voxel model, a cell construct and a fin ray, and what would calibrate it?
What one measurement on a real construct (strain amplitude against force) would bound the model's actuation parameter?
Can the composable, scenario and refused labels of the coupling record apply to an actuation-to-motion port?

projects.title: Epithelial repair patch
projects.goal: Ask one question about a cultured epithelial sheet: how do cell-level motility and mechanics set the closure of a gap, and what barrier geometry results?
projects.summary: A bounded proposal. Two published mechanics models define what is known. The Morpheus engine run here is named as a possible instrument. No wound simulation exists in this node yet.

context.base: Cultured epithelial monolayers. Lee and Wolgemuth model MDCK (dog kidney) wounds. Bai and Zeng model a generic three-dimensional epithelial monolayer on a substrate. No fish cell line or species parameter is used.
not_this: A clinical treatment or wound-care claim
Observed wound healing in any fish tissue

scales.role: Protrusion and contractility that drive cell motion (not modelled here)
Cell mechanics, cell-cell junctions and cell-substrate adhesion
Collective sheet motion, stress and closure
Patch-level barrier geometry: the shape and size of the remaining gap

tools.use: The Cellular Potts engine already run here, with receipts. A wound-gap setup would reuse the engine, not the example model.
tools.limit: The example model is a growth and cytokine feedback model, not a wound model.

tools.use: An algorithmic repair surrogate on a design raster.
tools.limit: Computed on a raster. It is not observed or simulated wound healing.

tools.use: A bioelectric patch with gap-junction controls, as one possible signaling channel.
Erk trigger waves on one regenerating zebrafish scale, as a signaling-wave example.
tools.limit: A signaling example from a different tissue. No coupling to motility is established.

virtual.name: Gap closure comparison on the Morpheus engine
virtual.status: proposed; no setup or result is in this node yet
virtual.plan: A gap geometry sweep with a motility ablation, a positive baseline, seeds and dt checks. Outputs: closure area, cell trajectories, mechanical cost, failure cases.

physical.name: Gap closure assay with live imaging
physical.plan: Image closure area over time in a monolayer, with a protrusion-inhibited arm, chosen and sourced before any run.
physical.needs: Edge stress by traction force microscopy, if the mechanical cost is to be compared.

sources.cite: Lee P, Wolgemuth CW (2011). Crawling cells can close wounds without purse strings or signaling. PLoS Comput Biol 7(3):e1002007.
sources.note: Abstract read from PubMed. Full text not read here.

sources.cite: Bai J, Zeng X (2023). Computational modeling and simulation of epithelial wound closure. Sci Rep 13:6265.
sources.note: Abstract read from PubMed. The PMC page was blocked by a bot check, so full text was not read here. Licence unknown: an independent review found no Creative Commons notice in a retrieved copy of the text, so none is claimed.

claims.text: In MDCK monolayers, wounds still close when a row of cells at the wound edge is deactivated. The authors' model captures closure dynamics and suggests wound healing is predominantly mechanical, modified but not produced by signaling.
claims.quote: modified, but not produced, by cell-cell signaling

claims.text: In a three-dimensional continuum finite-element model, closure efficiency is related to the initial gap size and to the intensity of lamellipodial protrusion. Wound-edge cells carry higher stress, and normal stress dominates shear stress.
claims.quote: closure efficiency is related to the initial gap size and the intensity of lamellipodial protrusion

missing_couplings: Signaling to motility or contractility: Lee and Wolgemuth conclude signaling modifies, but does not produce, closure (their model-based conclusion only). The Bai and Zeng abstract does not discuss signaling, so that coupling is an explicit gap there. Neither gives a transferable coupling.
Cell mechanics parameters for the chosen patch: none sourced here.
Continuum finite-element and Cellular Potts parameters are not interchangeable: no mapping exists.
Closure to barrier function (permeability): not modelled.
One cell line (MDCK) in one source and a generic monolayer in the other: no species transfer.

endpoints.text: In a declared stress-free, force-balanced model with no other active drive, setting protrusion intensity to zero leaves closed area constant to numerical tolerance.
endpoints.falsifier: Closure anyway triggers diagnosis, not a presumed defect: passive relaxation, initial stress, cell-cell or cell-substrate forces or another active mechanism can legitimately close a gap. No mechanism is read from the run until the cause is found.

endpoints.text: Closure efficiency changes with initial gap size and with protrusion intensity, as Bai and Zeng report. The abstract gives no direction, so none is assumed.
endpoints.falsifier: A run that shows no dependence on either does not reproduce the reported dependence.

endpoints.text: Paired runs from the same initial state give closed area within tolerance when dt (and grid, where there is one) is refined. Cell count is also preserved only under a declared no-birth, no-death assumption. Seed-to-seed variability is reported as an ensemble spread, not tested for equality.
endpoints.falsifier: A paired change larger than the tolerance voids the comparison for that setup. Variation across independent seeds is not by itself a defect.

open_questions: What evidence would connect a lower-scale prediction to tissue-scale closure in one named cell line? (The same shape of gap as the registered question F002.)
Is closure efficiency against gap size comparable between a Cellular Potts and a continuum model once both are calibrated to one measurement?
What barrier-geometry readout (remaining gap shape) is worth measuring beyond closed area?

other_projects_note: MorphoSwarm already holds other design projects (a pumpkin fruit, a newt and a toad) in its own checkout. They are not imported into this node, so none is shown here. The Studio shows two kinds of entry: a stored Project, which has an imported Project record, and an authored proposal, which has only a draft and is labelled as such. A project becomes stored when a Project record is imported and its entry names it.
